summary: boardcraft-desktop connect <loopback-port> <board-uuid> opens a read-only Windows Kit window. The view owns the identifier and masked password steps; EditClient signs in, resolves the in-memory session and reads the board off the UI thread. The existing host owns credential verification and board authorization.
evidence: windows_login_reject_retry passed in a real Windows process launched without a database URL or local actor. The driver used the visible Next and Sign in controls. An incorrect password showed Incorrect username or password with neither fixture row visible. Before allowing correction, fresh rustday_test connections found zero sessions and the original ordered rows: ID 42 Review sketch/1 and ID 17 Ink/1.

The fixture supplied the generated password through the child process's stdin after rejection. Entering it in the masked Kit input and submitting opened the read-only board. The driver checked both visible controls by item ID, label and vertical order, with the login controls gone. Independent reads found exactly one session linked to the expected Member and both ordered rows unchanged.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke -- --test-threads=1 passed all six cases, none filtered or ignored. The five inherited cases exercised entry, cancel, blur, Enter, failure actions, actor/board isolation, draft restoration and close/reopen on the developer path.
cargo test --locked --workspace passed all 18 portable tests. cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check passed.

Comparison used the existing-account reference observations in handoff 13 and the connected Android wrong-password journey in handoff 15. Windows likewise advanced locally, reported rejection at password submission and opened the protected board after correction. No fresh reference or Android device run was performed for this Windows packet. Windows token persistence, authenticated edits and graphical transport-fault recovery were not verified.
